newsitem.title: PERU: Freed diplomats complete job asked by Peru rebels.
newsitem.headline: Freed diplomats complete job asked by Peru rebels.

text.p: The diplomatic commission released by leftist rebels holding 400 hostages at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima has completed the tasks asked of it by the guerrillas, the ambassadors said on Friday.
"The ambassadors state they have now completed their mission," Canadian ambassador Anthony Vincent and Peruvian ambassador Armando Lecaros said in a joint statement.
After their release on Wednesday the commission of four diplomats had both ensured humanitarian aid for those inside the residence and had passed on to the government the rebels' demands, they said.
The two ambassadors remain "committed to the well-being and safety of the hostages," they said.
Athens had ordered home the Greek ambassador, Alcibiadis Karokis. The whereabouts of the commission's fourth member, the German ambassador, Heribert Woeckel, were unknown.

Michel Minning, a Swiss national of the Red Cross, was heading negotiations with the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) guerrillas, who stormed the compound in spectacular fashion on Tuesday night.
